display.title: Tanya Shiur 44: Chapter 33, Hashem Is Everywhere and the Joy of Being Near Him
display.summary_short: Two Yiddish Tanya classes on chapter 33: the young Baal Shem Tov alone in the forest, why we tell stories of tzaddikim, and the joy of knowing that the King of kings dwells with us.
display.summary_long: Shiur 44 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series holds two consecutive weekly classes on chapter 33. The first opens with the Alter Rebbe's new parable of the sun and its rays, then tells how the young Baal Shem Tov, found alone in the forest by an old man, explained that he was never alone, since his late father had taught him to fear nothing but Hashem. The rabbi explains why we tell stories of tzaddikim, linking sippur to sefirah and sapir: a story should make the listener shine, like a small man carried on a giant's shoulders. He then teaches that all creation is nullified before Hashem like a ray within the sun, adds Dovid HaMelech's 'closeness to Hashem is my good', the Twelve Pesukim, and the purpose of making a dwelling for Hashem below. The second class contrasts the finite and the Infinite, with the Rebbe's explanation that a one and a billion are equally nothing before the endless. It continues with the parable of a king who comes to live in a simple villager's hut, the words 'Ashreinu, how fortunate we are', and the Jewish inheritance from the Avos. The recording stops in the middle of a thought.
display.lesson: Hashem is truly everywhere and close to every Jew; thinking this through deeply brings a lasting joy that melts away every obstacle.

segments.title: First class: Tanya chapter 33, the sun and its rays
segments.summary: The Alter Rebbe's parable of the sun's rays shows how close a Jew is to Hashem, which brings great joy.

segments.title: The young Baal Shem Tov alone in the forest
segments.summary: An old man finds the boy alone in the woods, and he answers that he is never alone, as his father taught him to fear only Hashem.

segments.title: Why we tell stories of tzaddikim
segments.summary: A story should make the listener shine; like a small man on a giant's shoulders, we walk the road the tzaddikim opened.

segments.title: All creation nullified like a ray in the sun; a dwelling below
segments.summary: The world is as nothing before Hashem, closeness to Him is the greatest good, and this is the purpose of creation.

segments.title: Second class: Tanya chapter 33 continued
segments.summary: The finite and the Infinite, the joy of a dwelling for Hashem, and the inheritance of every Jew.

segments.title: One and a billion before the Infinite
segments.summary: From a maamar of the Rebbe: any number, however large, is equally nothing compared to the endless, so the highest and lowest worlds are alike before Hashem.

segments.title: The king who came to live in a villager's hut
segments.summary: A parable: how much more should we rejoice that the King of kings dwells with us when we do a mitzvah.

segments.title: Ashreinu: the inheritance of the Avos
segments.summary: Every Jew inherits the faith of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov, and the tzaddikim of past generations opened the way for us.

segments.title: Hashem is One, and nothing else exists
segments.summary: The plain and the Chassidic meaning of 'there is none else'; the recording breaks off here.
